text:
maya: folks — ran into a nasty onboarding repro on the sample Android app. tokens get refreshed concurrently and we end up re-sending the original request twice (or more). happens only on emulator / some Android devices.

samir: ugh, sounds like the classic auth race. which SDK versions + okhttp?

maya: repro on emulator Android 11, Retrofit 2.9.0, OkHttp 4.9.3 (we vendor a little). root message ts: 1934567890. stack snippet:```
W/OkHttp: HTTP FAILED: java.io.IOException: unexpected end of stream on Connection{10.0.2.2:8080, proxy=DIRECT hostAddress=/10.0.2.2:8080 cipherSuite=NONE} (recycle count 1)
java.io.IOException: authentication failed (token refresh kicked off)
```

ivy: can you paste the auth code? is refresh happening inside an Interceptor or Authenticator?

maya: we use an Interceptor+refresh via synchronized block but only tried naive double-check. simplified:```kotlin
class TokenInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val req = chain.request()
    val token = tokenStore.get()
    val withAuth = req.newBuilder().addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer $token").build()
    val resp = chain.proceed(withAuth)
    if (resp.code == 401) {
      // naive refresh:
      tokenRefresher.refreshBlocking() // blocks, replaces tokenStore
      return chain.proceed(req.newBuilder().addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer ${tokenStore.get()}").build())
    }
    return resp
  }
}
```

tony: that pattern is fine server-side but on Android with connection reuse it can cause the same underlying socket to be re-used while the refresh flow triggers another request that races. Interceptor-based refresh often ends up duplicating body streams.

samir: hmm. two immediate fixes: 1) use an OkHttp Authenticator instead of an interceptor so the client replays with new creds at the connection layer, or 2) centralize refresh with a single-flight lock and ensure only one network call performs the refresh and others wait and then retry.

maya: tried Authenticator but ran into a loop where the authenticator used the same client (and therefore the same authenticator) to call the token endpoint — infinite recursion.

ivy: classic. you need to call the token service with a separate OkHttpClient that has NO authenticator/interceptor attached. e.g.:```kotlin
val tokenClient = OkHttpClient.Builder().authenticator(null).build()
fun refreshBlocking(): String {
  val req = Request.Builder().url(tokenUrl).post(body).build()
  val r = tokenClient.newCall(req).execute()
  return parseToken(r)
}
```

tony: or simpler, use synchronized single-flight: an AtomicReference<CompletableFuture<String>> currentRefresh. if it's non-null, await it. The key is nobody should call chain.proceed() on the original request while the token body is being consumed elsewhere.

samir: also a practical workaround: set `Connection: close` header on requests that are sensitive to replay/stream consumption, or configure ConnectionPool to not reuse sockets for endpoints that do refreshes. Ugly but effective for short-term onboard app.

maya: onboarding sample app needs a minimal reproducible change. I'm going to: move refresh to a separate tokenClient + switch TokenInterceptor -> Authenticator and add single-flight guard. will push a patch to the sample repo.

ivy: when you push, add a note to README explaining why tokenClient exists — lots of new devs get caught here.

dev-bot: CI pipeline started for branch maya/auth-fix-sample (build #1024) :gear:

maya: thanks. quick checklist for the PR: mention emulator repro steps, include `adb logcat` snippet, and add a tiny unit/integration test that simulates concurrent 401s.

tony: and in SDK docs we should add a short section: "Android: Authenticator vs Interceptor — pitfalls and recommended patterns". I'll stub it out.

samir: can someone add an e2e flakiness test to catch duplicate upload/resend? we saw a couple of customer bugs triggered by this.

maya: will do. pushing patch in ~1h. can someone try the patch on a Pixel 3 emulator? I'm worried some OEMs behave differently with TLS/keepalive.

ivy: I can test on Pixel 3 and a physical Pixel 6 later today.

samir::+1:

maya: patch pushed: 1934567920-maya-auth-fix-sample PR. PTAL.

dev-bot: CI build #1024 passed :white_check_mark: (unit tests)

ivy: confirmed on Pixel 3 emulator — token refresh single-flight + separate token client fixes the dup request in the sample. no more 401 replay.

maya: awesome, will merge and backport to the sample release. thanks all :pray:
